title: If You Have A Dog, Read This 👆
body:
My dog died on an 83-degree day with the AC running. The vet said one sentence that made me realize I killed him without knowing it.

His name was Bear. He was six years old.

And I need to tell you what happened to him, because the thing that killed him is probably happening to your dog right now. And you have no idea. Just like I had no idea.

Bear was a Labrador mix with a head the size of a cantaloupe and a personality like a grumpy old man trapped inside a dog's body.

Deeply opinionated about everything. Personally offended by the vacuum cleaner. Convinced every couch cushion belonged to him and only him.

He slept at the foot of my bed every night. Same spot. Same heavy sigh when he settled in like the day had been impossibly hard. Same warm weight against my feet that I didn't appreciate enough until it was gone.

I'm 47. I live alone. Bear was my constant.

The kind of dog where you walk in the door after the worst day of your life and just sitting on the floor next to him for ten minutes makes it survivable.

I talked to him like he understood every word.

"You want the last bite?" "Do you think I should text him back?" "Don't judge me, it's cereal for dinner again."

He'd tilt his head and stare at me like he was forming an opinion.

If you're reading this, your dog is probably that for you.

So please keep reading. Because what I'm about to tell you could save his life.

I'd give anything — anything — to have read something like this eight months ago.

Every afternoon, Bear panted.

Not the dramatic, tongue-hanging, something-is-wrong kind.

Just a little heavier breathing than you'd expect from a dog lying on the living room floor in an air-conditioned house. The kind you glance at and think: "He's a dog. Dogs pant. It's warm out."

He moved around a lot too.

Couch to the carpet. Carpet to the hallway. Hallway to the bathroom.

He'd circle, lie down, stay for maybe twenty minutes, then get up and do it all over again. Not frantically. Not like something was wrong. Just… never quite settled.

And the bathroom tile.

Every single day, by early afternoon, Bear was sprawled on the bathroom floor. I used to joke about it. "He's in his office again." My friends laughed. I laughed.

It wasn't funny.

I noticed all of it. The panting. The moving. The tile. I saw every single sign.

I just didn't know what I was looking at.

The day it happened was a Tuesday in August. 83 degrees.

Not the kind of heat that makes the news. Just a normal warm day.

I topped off his water before work. Set the AC to 74. Kissed him on his big dumb head. Told him I'd be home by six.

Checked the camera around lunch. He was on the bathroom tile. Sleeping.

I smiled and put my phone away.

I got home at ten past six.

The house was wrong.

I knew it the second I opened the door. Not the usual quiet — the kind where he'd already be there, tail going, slamming into my legs before I could put my bag down.

This was a different kind of quiet. The kind where something is missing.

I called his name.

Nothing.

I found him on the kitchen tile. On his side. Eyes half open.

I don't remember picking him up.

I remember the weight of him — sixty-two pounds of dead weight in my arms. I remember he was still warm. I remember saying his name over and over and over, like if I said it enough times he'd blink.

I wrapped him in the throw blanket from the couch. The one he always tried to steal.

Drove to the emergency vet. I don't remember the drive. I remember the fluorescent lights in the parking lot. The sliding doors. A tech taking him from my arms.

She came back eleven minutes later. I know because I watched the clock the entire time.

"I'm so sorry. He's gone. It was heatstroke."

I said the AC was on. I said it was only 83 degrees. I said I did everything right.

She told me she'd lost three dogs that week. Same thing. Every owner said the same words I just said.

The bill was $3,800. For eleven minutes and a dead dog.

I sat in the parking lot for a long time after. Engine running. AC on.

I remember thinking: the AC was on for Bear too.

The vet called the next morning.

She said she wanted to explain what happened. That most owners never get this explanation.

"Your AC was working fine," she said. "The air in your house was 74 degrees. But that's not where Bear was overheating."

She explained it simply. And I will never forget it.

A dog's body temperature sits around 101°F.

Every surface he lies on — the carpet, the couch, the tile, his bed — absorbs that heat. Within minutes, the surface underneath him warms up. And once it's absorbed enough body heat, it stops pulling heat away. It just holds it there. Pressed against his belly and chest.

Then she said the sentence that changed everything:

"Think about when you flip your pillow to the cool side at night. You do it because your body heat has warmed it up and it's not comfortable anymore. That's what Bear was doing every time he got up and moved spots. He was flipping the pillow. Except you can't flip a floor."

That was it. That was the sentence.

And every single thing I'd watched Bear do for five years suddenly made sense.

The panting every afternoon? His body trying to cool itself because the surface underneath him had stopped helping.

The moving from spot to spot? Him searching for any surface that hadn't absorbed his heat yet.

The bathroom tile? Denser. Takes longer to warm up. But it warms up too. Eventually, there's nowhere left to go.

Then she said the part that broke me:

"This isn't a certain-breeds thing. It's not just Bulldogs and Pugs. It's not just old dogs or overweight dogs. It's physics. Every dog runs at 101 degrees internally. Every surface absorbs heat. Every dog lying on any surface in your house is dealing with this. Most of the time they cope. But it's a slow accumulation of stress. And sometimes, on the wrong day, it crosses a line you didn't know was there."

That's what haunts me.

It didn't look like an emergency. It looked like a normal dog on a normal afternoon.

And that's exactly why I missed it.

I didn't sleep much in the weeks after he died. I read everything. Joined every dog group. Called two other vets.

And I started understanding why everything I'd been doing — everything every dog owner does — doesn't actually solve the problem.

The AC? Cools the air three feet above your dog. Does nothing for the surface underneath him. Bear was generating 101 degrees of body heat directly into the carpet. The AC can't reach that.

Gel cooling mats? Absorbs heat for 20–30 minutes, then it's full. Just a warm mat with chemical gel that eventually punctures and leaks.

Wet towels? Body-temperature warm within ten minutes. Then they trap moisture and heat against the dog like an insulating blanket. Actually worse than bare floor.

Every solution out there either cools the air or absorbs heat until it can't anymore.

None of them do the one thing that actually matters: move heat away from the dog's body continuously, without ever stopping.

The vet told me: "The answer isn't colder air. It's a surface that doesn't absorb heat and hold it. A surface that conducts heat away. Continuously. One that doesn't reach a point where it stops working."

That's it. That's what would have saved Bear.

I found it at 2 AM on a Thursday in October, scrolling through a Dog Mom group with swollen eyes and cold coffee on the nightstand.

A woman named Sarah. She'd lost her Staffy to the same thing — heatstroke, indoors, AC running — two years earlier. Her post wasn't selling anything. She was sharing what she'd learned since.

She described her new dog's behavior: "He used to pant every afternoon and I thought nothing of it. He'd drift from spot to spot, never settling. Since the mat, he picks one spot and stays there for hours. The afternoon panting is gone."

Someone asked what she was using.

PawLabs Cooling Mat.

Not a gel mat. Not a water mat. Not something you freeze. An ice-silk fabric that conducts heat away from the dog's body continuously — instead of absorbing it and warming up like every other surface.

If the problem is surfaces that absorb and trap heat, the solution is a surface that moves heat away without ever stopping. No gel to saturate. No water to evaporate. No freezing. No setup. Just physics.

I wasn't ready for another dog. Not even close.

But I ordered it that night. Because when I was ready, it needed to be there from day one.

It arrived three days later. I put it on the living room floor where Bear's bed used to be.

Three months later, I brought Murphy home.

Same breed. Same big head. Same heavy sigh when he lies down.

People asked how I could do it. Same breed. After what happened.

I told them: because I know something now that I didn't know before. And this time, I'm ready.

The PawLabs mat was already on the floor. Had been for weeks.

First warm day with Murphy, I watched him like I'd never watched anything in my life.

Hour 1: He sniffed the mat. Circled once. Lay down. I sat on the couch and waited for the panting to start. Nothing. Asleep within minutes. Breathing slow and steady. I put my hand on the mat next to him — after a full hour with a 60-pound dog on it, still cool. Not cold-from-the-fridge cold. But noticeably, unmistakably cool.

Hour 2: He hadn't moved. On the carpet, Bear would have relocated twice by now. Murphy was in the same spot. No panting.

Hour 4: Still there. I touched the mat right next to his belly. Cool. The carpet six inches away? Warm from the air. The mat was not.

End of day: I realized I'd been holding my breath since morning. The afternoon panting that started at 2 PM every day with Bear? It never came. The restless spot-switching? Murphy didn't do it. He picked his spot on the mat and stayed.

Week 2: I took Murphy to the vet for his first check-up. Same clinic. Same vet who called me the morning after Bear died. She checked his temperature, listened to his heart. "He's doing beautifully." I told her about the mat. She nodded. "That makes sense. If the surface is conducting heat away continuously, the cycle I described to you after Bear never gets a chance to start."

The first time I noticed — really noticed — I sat on the floor next to him and cried.

Not sad crying. The kind that comes when you finally understand something that came too late for one dog but not too late for another.

I still run the AC. Still fill the water bowl. Still make frozen treats on weekends because Murphy completely loses his mind for them.

But I don't check the camera twelve times a day anymore. I don't lie awake wondering if he's okay. The knot in my stomach when I leave for work — it's gone.

Not because I stopped caring. Because I finally addressed the one thing I didn't know was killing Bear.

I'm writing this because I sat in that vet's parking lot with the engine running and promised myself I'd tell every dog owner I could.

If your dog pants in the afternoon — even a little. If he switches spots and you've never really thought about why. If he always ends up on the tile. Even if none of it looks like a big deal.

It probably isn't. Today.

But it's his body telling you the surface underneath him has absorbed his heat and stopped doing its job. And that stress adds up. Day after day. Summer after summer.

I keep one in the living room and one in Murphy's crate. No freezing. No water. No setup. Just a surface that does what you think your floor already does — but doesn't stop.

Here's what I wish someone told me about the money:

I spent $3,800 at the emergency vet that night. For eleven minutes. For nothing.

The PawLabs mat costs less than a single vet visit. Less than a gel mat that stops working after half an hour. Less than what most of us spend on dog toys in a year.

And they do a 30-day money-back guarantee. If I'm wrong — if you put the mat down and your dog keeps panting, keeps switching spots, keeps seeking the tile — you get every penny back. No questions.

But if I'm right, and your dog is showing you even one of the signs Bear showed me, you'll wish you hadn't waited.

One more thing: these mats sell out every single year before summer. Every year. By the time it's actually hot and you're watching your dog pant on the kitchen floor, they're gone and you're on a waitlist. Last summer I tried to buy a second one for my sister. Sold out for six weeks.

Right now they're running their pre-summer sale. Once summer hits, the price goes up. The best price you'll get is before you need it. Not after.

Murphy's on his right now. Same spot where Bear used to lie. Head between his paws. Snoring. Not panting. Not moving. Just settled.

I can hear him breathing.

And for the first time since that Tuesday in August, I'm not afraid of what I'll come home to.

Don't wait for your Tuesday.

title: Trusted by 10,000+ cat shelters
body:
I TESTED 11 different pheromone diffusers across our intake cats and guess what? 10 showed ZERO measurable change in spraying behavior within 30 days. Two cats actually got WORSE on the most popular brand.

I know that sounds like an ad. It's not.

I'm Amanda Torres. I've been running the behavioral rehabilitation program at North Bridge Cat Rescue for 9 years. Over 1,400 cats through this program. Most of them surrendered for one reason: spraying and urine marking that destroy their home.

For years, when adopters asked which diffuser to use at home, I gave the same lazy answer: "Whatever your vet recommends should be fine."

That was before Diana.

She adopted Pepper from us eight months ago. Sweet cat. Calm. Perfect behavioral history. We sent her home with one highlighted instruction in her discharge notes: continue the maternal pheromone protocol (yes, it’s our fault to not be clear) 

So she used the diffuser her vet recommended.

Feliway Optimum. The purple box. The one every vet hands out at checkout.

She followed every instruction perfectly. Plugged it in day one. New refill every 30 days. Did everything right.

Pepper started spraying the couch within two weeks. Then the bedroom wall. Then the laundry pile. Diana bought a SECOND Feliway unit because the first one "must not be strong enough."

The spraying got worse. 

She came in to surrender him four months later, sobbing.

"I got him neuteured. I placed 3 litter box around the house. I bought every product they told me to buy. How did this happen?"

I pulled Pepper's file. Page two, highlighted in yellow: continue maternal pheromone protocol.

She assumed Feliway covered it.

It doesn't. And I had never been specific enough to say so.

I felt sick.

Because Diana was not the first. I had sent dozens of cats home with adopters who went straight to their vet, followed every instruction, and came back 6 months later with the same story. Different cat. Same purple box. Same result.

So I did something I should have done years earlier.

I started testing every major pheromone diffuser I could find. Amazon bestsellers. Chewy top-rated. Vet-recommended brands.

Out of 11 diffusers I tested across cats in our rehabilitation program. 8 showed no change at all by day 14. 10 produced NO measurable reduction in spraying within 30 days (some of them even show hardware failure like product leaks / oily residue).  Two cats on one of the most popular brands were spraying MORE by week three than on the day they arrived.

Only one came back with a different result.

I was actually shocked. I even ran it across two separate intake groups just to be sure.

Every other diffuser uses HEAT to release pheromone into the air. Heat destroys the pheromone before it ever leaves the unit. Whatever reaches your cat is already broken. That is why week one sometimes looks better, then stops. The signal was never whole.

The second problem is the pheromone type. The popular brands use a TERRITORIAL signal, the same scent a cat uses to claim space. When your cat detects it, the brain reads: another cat moved in. So instead of calming your cat, it tells his brain there is a stranger in the house. That is why some cats spray MORE on Feliway. Not a fluke. Exactly what the biology predicts.

Päw Care uses the calming pheromone a mother cat sends her kittens from the first day of life. And it delivers it WITHOUT heat, so the signal arrives whole.

I told Diana to bring Pepper back. Not to surrender him. Just to let me try something.

Day 3: marked twice. Down from his usual eight or nine times a day.
Day 11: one mark. And it was half-hearted, like he forgot why he was doing it.
Day 21: NONE 

Diana walked in to pick him up. She stood in the doorway and started crying after I show her the result.

I've seen it happen too many times to call it a miracle. It is what happens when you finally give a cat the signal its brain has been scanning for.

Such a relief, definitely recommend for anxious kitties.  I cannot explain what it felt like to have my home back.”

"My cat seems noticeably calmer and less stressed, especially in situations that used to trigger anxiety. One of the biggest improvements has been a reduction in unwanted behaviors like urine spraying and general tension between pets in the household. The environment feels much more peaceful overall."

title: Read next chapter👉🏻
body:
Chapter 1
Ava's POV

Like most girls, I always picture my high-school prom. I'm no exception. My friends and I are gearing up to go dress shopping, but my parents just can't seem to grasp how much this matters to me! They insist I stay away from anything that might damage my image or draw negative attention to our family name.

Apparently, being the beta's daughter means I'm kept on a tight leash when it comes to having fun. Naturally, I use every chance I get to enjoy myself and live my life to the absolute fullest.

My mom tells me I remind her of who she was before she found her mate, so she tends to cut me a little slack, but my dad is an intense enforcer of the rules.

My mom, Gwen, stands 5' 6" with a toned body and light brown hair that falls to her chest. She's a warrior in our pack, and she started teaching me how to fight when I was five. My dad, Gideon, is 6' 7" with a football-player build that looks like he could bench a car. Ink covers him from head to toe, and he has slick black hair. He never takes it easy on me, and he's annoyed that I'm not a boy, but that never stops him from raising me like one anyway.

I take part in every competition that the boys take part in, yet I still can't manage to beat him when he's at his best. He believes I'm good enough and that I should earn the second position when he steps down—if I can straighten up and stop giving him headaches. I start laughing as I remember all the lectures he has delivered to me over the years.

“What mate would want a girl who parties and is fast and loose with the rules? Especially an Alpha — who would ever want you as his beta?” I laugh, because I grew up with the future alpha, Kaelen.

He's my best friend, and once in a while we kiss, but I'm saving myself for my mate. Kaelen is 6' 8" of pure muscle with short black hair, and he wears a tribal tattoo that runs from his chest to his shoulder, wraps around his neck and arm, and stretches across his back.

With piercing, bright blue eyes, he's basically sex on a stick. His temper fits his bad-boy appearance, but he always has a soft spot for me. I've known for a long time that I've always held his attention.

At 5' 7" with a slender, toned figure, waist-length dark wavy hair, and emerald green eyes, I tend to catch more than a few guys' attention. Still, I think most of them only look at me because they assume they can earn the beta position, so I usually ignore them.

"Hurry up, Ava!" my best friend Serena shouts. She's stunning, with creamy mocha skin and shoulder-length black hair. Even though she's only 5' 5", she carries herself like she's eight feet tall. I hop up from my vanity and sprint to the front door before she decides to climb the stairs. I kept her waiting once before, and she nearly tore my door off its hinges!

"Coming! I gotta finish my makeup," I say, a little breathless.

"Finn, Kaelen, and Garrett are already in the car waiting for us." Finn is another warrior's son. He's 6' 6" with pale skin, hazel eyes, and shoulder-length blond hair. He's attractive in his own way, but there's a softer look about him. He always has eyes for Serena, even though she never pays him any attention.

Since she's the gamma's daughter, she gets the same lectures I get. Garrett is her brother and Kaelen's right-hand man, since the two of them were born only a few days apart. He's 6' 6" and darker than Serena, with jet-black hair and the same dark brown eyes she has—those eyes with a gold fleck in them that they inherited. Apparently, it's just one of their family traits.

"Bye, Mom and Dad!"

"Bye, honey. Behave, and mind-link me if anything happens! And don't get into a fight this time!" Dad yells from the kitchen. It only happened once, and I won, so it wasn't my fault the guy couldn't understand the word no.

Dad isn't overly worried this time because I promised the boys are with us and can "protect us." Like I need a guy to protect me. I roll my eyes and step outside with my arm draped over Serena's shoulders.

"Hurry up, girls! I am not free all day long," Garrett yells.

"Oh, shut up, Garrett—you've got nothing but time today," Serena snaps back as she slides into the back seat of Kaelen's Cadillac Escalade. Naturally, I climb straight into the front passenger seat next to Kaelen. Some people assume Kaelen is my mate. We don't think so, but we aren't against it either. I'm treated like it, and I never really mind.

"I should be the one up front. My legs are way longer than yours, Ava, and if we have to jump out fast and fight, I need better access than the third row," Finn complains.

"Oh yeah? Want another rematch, Finn?" I raise an eyebrow at him. The last time he questioned me, I dropped him more times than he could count, and he still claims he "lets me win."

Everyone bursts out laughing except Kaelen, who just lifts an eyebrow at Finn. Finn is an excellent warrior, but when beta blood runs through your veins and you've trained since you were five, not many people can really measure up.

"I'm only trying to be a gentleman, Ava. I'd like to treat you like the princess you are," Finn teases.

All he earns from me is a snort and an eye roll—and from Kaelen, a growl deep in his chest.

"Anyway," Serena smirks, "what kind of dress do you want to get today?"

"Hm," I ponder, "maybe a skin-tight one that stops right below my ass, with a deep V-neck that's sheer."

"Like hell you are!" Kaelen growls.

I laugh so hard I almost choke. "I'm kidding—jeez. I honestly don't know. But I do want one that's floor length!"

"Well, I want a short one that makes my legs look longer and hugs my curves."

"Serena, mom and dad will kill you—you know that, right?" Garrett asks, dragging a hand down his face. "You're going to be what gets me killed," he mutters, and with our wolf hearing, every one of us hears him.

"I'm their princess—they won't! And besides, if I find my mate, they can't say a thing!" Serena says, her eyes hard with determination. I recognize that look; once she has it, there's no changing her mind.

Our "prom" isn't really a prom, exactly. It starts as a traditional prom, but over the years every unmated eighteen-year-old begins crashing other packs' prom nights, hoping to find their mate—or, if not, at least score a quick lay.

My birthday is the day before prom, only a week away, and I'm thrilled. At last, I get to find out whether Kaelen is my mate or not. Every time I think about it, a strange sensation twists in my stomach.

What if he isn't my mate and he ends up choosing another girl? Would I actually be okay with that? Deep down, I always like the way he protects me, but he does it so I can still smack a guy around, while he watches closely to make sure I don't get hurt while I'm at it.

Chapter 2
Ava's POV

"Everything alright, kitten?" Kaelen asks in a low, quiet voice. I'm so wrapped up in my thoughts that I don't even notice the chatter in the back fading away, and he picks up on the fact that I don't toss out my usual sarcastic remark toward them.

Kitten is the name he started calling me when we were kids because, supposedly, my temper and feisty attitude didn't quite fit my small size. I didn't hit my growth spurt until I was fourteen, so the nickname ended up staying.

"Yeah, I'm okay," I say with a sigh.

"No matter what happens, it's going to be okay—I'll never forget you," he mind-links, making sure no one else can overhear. I turn my head toward him and offer a sad little smile. He says it every time, but I know that once he finds his mate, she will be the only thing on his mind, and she won't want us to stay as close as we are now.

I'll understand it, but that doesn't mean it won't hurt like a bitch. You don't learn who your mate is until you're both eighteen, so even though Kaelen is nineteen, we still won't know until next Friday.

"Yay, we're here!" Serena shrieks, yanking Kaelen and me right out of our private exchange. My excitement floods back instantly.

After six stores, I finally step out wearing a breathtaking deep red silk gown. It's cut with a sweetheart neckline and a corset-style bodice that clings to my hips and ass before flowing down. A daring high slit puts my toned thigh on perfect display.

The moment I hear people gasp, I lift my gaze and find everyone staring like their jaws have dropped to the floor. I'm not stupid—I know exactly how good I look and how to make an entrance, and this dress makes a pure statement from top to bottom. Kaelen is the first to recover, letting out a low growl, and everyone immediately closes their mouths and looks away.

"OMG, Ava, that dress is made for you," Serena says once she finally comes out too. She's in a short, thigh-length royal blue satin dress. The way it wraps around her again and again makes her look like a goddess, giving her curves and legs for days—especially paired with her silver peep-toed heels.

"Thanks," I say with a bright grin. "Yours looks incredible on you too!"

"Well, it covers more than I thought it would," Garrett mutters, still unhappy about how short it is.

"Alright, boys—time to pay and go find tuxes for all of you!" I announce.

Then, as I step back into the fitting room to strip out of the dress, Kaelen's voice suddenly slides into my head. "Kitten, don't get too attached to that dress, because even if I'm not your mate, I'll be ripping it off you on Saturday night."

I smirk, heat rushes to my cheeks, and my panties turn instantly wet. "And who says I'm going to let you?" I shoot back, teasing. "I'll come up behind you, slam you against a wall, and take you right here, woman," he fires right back. "This whole store is about to smell how turned on I am—do you want that?" I shoot back, struggling to regain control of myself. The only response I get is his amused chuckle.

"Come on, boys, let's get started on those tuxes," Kaelen says aloud. "Hurry up, girls—we'll be on the other side of the store!"

"Ass," I mind-link him, not even trying to hide it.

Once we change back, Serena and I meet up with the boys, and they're already done, so we start heading home. In the back seat, Finn, Serena, and Garrett argue over who the better dancer is, while I end up staring out the window, drifting off. I feel like my entire life is going to shift in a week, and I can't even explain why. I just can't shake this bad feeling. I've always had this weird knack for knowing things—like sensing when something terrible is coming or when someone is lying.

Maybe I'm just tuned into nature or something, but I feel calmer when I can run or be in the woods. Maybe that's why the ominous feeling keeps growing inside me. I need to take a walk through the woods around our pack territory. When we finally pull in at home, I quickly tell everyone I'm tired and that I'm calling it a night.

Luckily, my parents still aren't home, so I stash my dress and head out for a walk. The sky is darkening, and I love this part of the day. Dusk is gorgeous, with reds and oranges brushing color across the horizon. It's late April and the weather is warming up, but I still grab a jacket anyway.

I hate feeling cold, and April evenings at dusk are still a little chilly. There's a small meadow I love about half a mile from my house. I like to stretch out there and stare up at the stars. A small break in the canopy lets sunbeams or moonlight slip down through. Even though the stars aren't fully out yet, I still lie there and let my thoughts wander—until a stick snaps and the scent of coconut and rainwater floods my nose.

Kaelen.

"I knew something was off with you."

"I don't know what you're talking about."

"Oh really? This is the place you run to whenever you're stressed about something, so tell me, kitten."

I let out a sigh. He knows me far too well. "I just have this feeling that something bad is going to happen next Saturday. There are going to be like five hundred kids coming here from all over for the prom. Things are going to change. I just don't know if it's going to be for the better."

Kaelen knows about the "feeling" I get. More than once, my instincts were never wrong, and they saved us once or twice. He lowers himself beside me and stays silent for a while. The stars are out now, and they look beautiful.

"I've always liked you, and I've always admired you. You would make the perfect Luna, and I'd be proud if you were my mate. Even if we aren't mates, we'll find a way to make it work. I'll be jealous of any mate you have who isn't me, but as long as you're happy, that's what matters."

"If only it were that easy," I say softly. I know we've talked about this more than once, and we've messed around too, but if we aren't mates, it's going to break my heart. I've wanted him as my mate in secret ever since we were little.

"Do you think it's something else that's going to happen?"

"I just don't know."

"Kitten…"

Right then, my mom pushes through the mind-link. "Honey, where are you? We just got home."

"I went for a walk. I'll be right there!" I reply, and I shut the mind-link down. I turn back to Kaelen, and he can already tell it's time for me to go.

"It's fine. We'll finish this conversation later, okay?"

"Alright." I flash him a small smile, and then I go home.

Chapter 3
Ava's POV

"Ava! Wake up, or you'll miss the start of school!" my mother calls up from the lower floor. Damn—it's Monday, and the weekend passed in an instant. My final year is nearly over. The prom is scheduled for this Saturday, and graduation follows the Saturday after. I turn onto my side, and getting out of bed is definitely the hardest part of my day.

My bed and I share a profoundly dedicated, affectionate bond. I step quickly into the shower, then pull on my clothes at top speed. Normally, I choose comfortable clothes, but because training is on my agenda today, I allow my hair to dry naturally and pull on leggings, a sports bra, and a cropped shirt.

"AVA! Your friends are outside waiting for you!" Mom shouts once more, exactly as an urgent car horn sounds from the road. For as long as I can recall, Serena and Garrett have collected me and driven us all to school. Walking would take just ten minutes, but it's a welcome relief not to make the trip in the cold. Clutching a granola bar, I approach the door where Mom is standing; she offers me a broad smile, draws me close, and embraces me before I leave.

Jogging down the steps of my wraparound porch, I can immediately hear them quarreling as though they've been locked in debate for hours.

"Garrett, I already told you, I am perfectly capable of deciding for myself!" Serena exclaims, angry. For as long as I can remember, Garrett has been excessively protective of her. He disapproves of her training, her flirting, her dating—anything he believes could send the wrong signal to a guy. He prefers her to live like a princess who never needs to do any work. Regrettably for him, Serena is deeply devoted to combat, and her temperament matches that perfectly. In that sense, she and I could practically be identical.

"Are the two of you already arguing? What's the reason this time?" I ask, intervening.

"Garrett believes I should remain at home learning to cook or working at the daycare rather than heading to the field after school for training," Serena retorts sharply. "According to him, it lets guys stare at something that doesn't belong to them, and it isn't appropriate for a lady. It doesn't matter that I can protect myself or that I rank among the best female fighters," she says, her irritation overflowing.

"Garrett, you are aware you still haven't won this dispute and you never will," I inform him, supporting her. "She will do as she wishes, and you must accept her as she is instead of trying to mold her into some obedient trophy wife." I am defending my closest friend, partly because I adore her—but also because I absolutely reject ever being forced into that box myself.

"Whatever," Garrett mumbles quietly, and he accelerates his Dodge Charger violently as if it had personally insulted him.

Finally, the school day concludes, and I can at last direct my frustration onto someone's face. I sprint directly to the field, and I notice my dad walking out to begin training. He gives me a brief nod, then shouts for everyone to start with ten warm-up laps, after which we are to pair up and practice offense and defense. During my second lap, I suddenly sense someone approaching from behind.

"Hey there, good looking." The smell of coconut and rain washes over me. I don't even have to glance back to know Kaelen's eyes are fixed on my backside as I run. I roll my eyes, then abruptly cut to the right and kick my foot out, tripping him and sending him stumbling forward.

But Kaelen is now past eighteen and he has his wolf, so he lands smoothly without a flicker of surprise—and he glances back at me and winks. He slows to match my pace and observes me, and this time I nearly stumble. The look he gives me is filled with such intense love, wanting, and painful yearning that my throat goes tight. I can't even summon my usual sharp reply to toss at him.

"Cat got your tongue?" he inquires.

"Oh, just this arrogant future alpha believes he's all that," I reply.

He pretends to be hurt, places a hand over his heart, and adopts a wounded look. "Well then," he states, "I suppose you ought to be my partner and demonstrate precisely how arrogant I am."

"Sure," I say to him. "I would be delighted to take you down a notch or two, mister."

When we complete our laps, everyone separates into pairs and we begin sparring. Kaelen understands I need to release pent-up frustration, so he begins on defense. I connect with a few firm punches, but I'm the one who ultimately feels more pain. Even though I am the top female fighter, I still cannot truly compete with a future alpha. Nevertheless, I do feel improved, and I eventually succeed in shedding some of the stress I've been holding. The feelings leading up to this Saturday grow more intense each day.

"Are you feeling any better, kitten?" he asks.

"No," I confess. "It only continues to intensify. The emotions become stronger each day."

Kaelen appears sincerely concerned. He glances behind me, then lowers his head.

"Ava! We must discuss your birthday party on Friday, as well as Serena's," the Luna announces. Since Serena and I have the same birthday, we always hold a joint celebration. We are both thrilled because we will receive our wolves and we may finally encounter our mates!

"Yes, Luna!" I reply promptly. "I had an idea—since the prom is the following day—why don't we have a small gathering before the prom, and then we can all proceed to the dance together?"

"Excellent, dear. I will organize everything for you!" she says kindly.

"Thanks, Mom!" Kaelen calls to his mother. The Luna is the kindest person I have ever known. She stands just over 5' 4" with a small build and long blond hair, and she is gorgeous. Those blue eyes of Kaelen's certainly come from her. I don't believe she even knows how to raise her voice.

I watch Elara walk away, and my mind turns to the Alpha—the most frightening person I know. He is only slightly taller than Kaelen, constructed of solid muscle, completely bald, and he has a stare that makes you uncomfortable even without projecting his aura.

How those two ever ended up together is beyond me.

"So, will you accompany me to the prom, Ava?" Kaelen asks, pulling me from my thoughts.

"You certainly took your time asking," I tell him. "What if I already secured a date?"

"Please," he responds. "Everybody knows you are mine. No one would risk inviting you without checking with me first."

"Is that so? And what exactly makes you believe I belong to you?" I challenge.

"Don't make me laugh, kitten. I claimed you when you were five," he states.

"Yeah, well, we'll find out on Friday, won't we?" I retort.

"About that…" Kaelen unexpectedly steps back and rubs the back of his neck.

"What?" I ask, immediately wary.

"Dad has me attending several meetings with alphas whose teenagers are coming to the prom, so I'm occupied on Friday. I won't be able to see you until Saturday at the party."

"What the hell? Are you serious?" I snap. "That's just perfect. How long have you known this without telling me?" My eyes sting with tears. I am angry—more than angry. And that's what I despise most about myself: whenever I become furious, I cry.

"I just found out, I swear!" Kaelen asserts. "I'm truly sorry, Ava. I really wish we could have discovered whether we are mates before the party so we could have planned what would happen. I didn't plan this." He gazes at me as though he is begging—as though he needs me to comprehend.

But as I turn away and begin walking off, only one idea occupies my mind: this marks the beginning of a truly terrible week.

Chapter 4
Ava's POV

I have not seen Kaelen at all throughout this week because I am completely overwhelmed with studying and completing every remaining assignment so that I do not need to attend school next week. I am enrolled in all advanced courses, and I have a strong suspicion I won't want to set foot in the school building next week, so Serena and I work extremely hard and finish everything.

"Are you excited about our birthdays tomorrow?" Serena squeals.

I turn over in my bed and respond, "Absolutely yes! I am incredibly eager to meet my wolf! I keep wondering how big she is, what color she is, and what her name will be."

"Me too! I am so happy your parents allowed me to sleep over tonight—I am glad we get to experience this together."

"Well, we've been working tirelessly all week so we don't have to go to school today or next week!"

Serena's expression abruptly becomes solemn. "What will you do if Kaelen is not your mate?" She is aware of all my thoughts and worries because I share everything with her.

With a deep sigh, I answer, "I truly do not know. Let's just go to sleep. I have a sense tomorrow is going to be a very lengthy day."

'Wake up, sleepy head!' a voice suddenly screams inside my mind. For a moment, I believe I am still dreaming. 'I am not a dream, girl! WAKE UP!' I jerk my eyes open and realize I have my wolf now!

'Oh my god! What is your name? What color are you? I already love you!' I exclaim. I am attempting to remain still so I do not wake Serena, but my excitement is uncontrollable.

I hear light giggles. 'My name is Sable, and you will see what color I am when we shift!'

'Damn—can I shift right now?'

'You're so impatient,' Sable remarks, 'but yes, you can. It's going to hurt like hell, but I will guide you through it.'

As quietly as I can, I climb out of bed, tiptoe down the hallway, and slip outside. 'Okay, now what?'

'Go into the woods. You will probably want to remove your clothes and get comfortable—this will require some time.'

Thirty minutes later, fire tears through my entire body. I bite down on my tongue to keep from screaming and letting everyone know I'm here. Then my bones begin to snap. 'SABLE, what is happening?' I panic.

'Picture your hands as paws, and picture yourself as a wolf,' Sable directs. 'I know it hurts, but it will not last long. You can do this!' I curl into a fetal position, listening to my bones break, and then suddenly I am staring at the ground. I smell damp soil and a thousand scents I do not even have names for. When I look down, I see paws—dark brown with a reddish tint. I lift my head and look around, and everything appears clearer, brighter, louder, and flooded with smells I never noticed before.

"Wow." That is honestly all I can say at this moment.

Sable laughs. 'Let's run!' And we do. We arrive at a stream, and I look down at my reflection. Sable is beautiful. She possesses my emerald green eyes, and her dark brown fur carries this subtle reddish tint. We run for hours before we finally return to my parents' house.

"You should shift back and sleep. You will need rest for today!"

"Um, exactly how do I do that, Sable?"

'Just imagine yourself as human again,' she says, mentally rolling her eyes at me.

I do as she says, and suddenly cold air hits my skin. I glance down and realize I am naked, so I swiftly pull my clothes back on. When I slip into bed again, exhaustion washes over me like a powerful wave.

'You will feel tired for the rest of the day,' Sable informs me, 'but also—Happy Birthday!'

'Thank you, Sable! Goodnight!'

"OH GOD, OH GOD!" I hear high-pitched shrieking, and I bolt upright in bed. I push hair away from my face and look around to see Serena bouncing and screaming as if she is about to explode. My heart races as I try to understand what is happening, but before I can ask Serena what on earth is going on, my parents burst into the room—nearly tearing the door from its hinges.

"What happened? What is wrong?" my mom asks us.

"I got my wolf! Oh, she is so sarcastic and funny! She is just like me, and we cannot wait to find our mate!"

Serena sings, spinning in circles like a small child who just received ice cream.

"What is her name?" Serena asks.

I cannot wait to tell my parents about Sable.

"Is she always this loud?" Sable asks, sounding both amused and irritated.

"Yeah," I answer her silently, "that is just Serena—an enormous personality contained in a small body."

"Zephyr! I cannot wait to shift and see what she looks like!"

"After breakfast, Serena! You'll need energy for that!" Mom gently scolds, but she is smiling, so we know she is no longer alarmed. "This calls for chocolate chip pancakes!"

I hear Dad grumbling that he never gets waffles anymore, and I hear Mom laugh while she tells him not to be difficult. As tough and stern as he is, he always has a soft spot for me and my mom.

"My wolf's name is Sable! She is just like me too, and she has brown fur with a red tint to it!" I announce.

"You already shifted?" Serena asks, her face falling with disappointed sadness. "I thought we were going to shift together." With a dramatic sigh, she sits down on the bed. I scoot over to her and wrap her in a hug.

"I did not mean to hurt your feelings. Sable woke me up last night, and I simply could not wait. I do not have a lot of energy, but I would love to shift again with you and go for a short run!"

"Oh, yes please! Maybe our mate is out there. I could use some sexy time with my mate," Sable sings, twirling around in my head. "Girl, please—control your thoughts," I silently scold back, rolling my eyes. If her thoughts are as intense as mine…

"Okay, yeah, that is fine," Serena says, making peace with it. "I am not really angry—just disappointed. I understand though. I probably would have done the same thing." She always imagines we will do everything simultaneously: shift together, find our mates together, get pregnant together, all of it.

I never really feel like life works that neatly, but I never voice that to crush her dreams. Honestly, I do not want to. I also wish for us to experience everything together, but but it never feels quite right—as if it's not supposed to line up perfectly.

"Girls! Breakfast!" Mom yells from the kitchen. Serena shoves me onto the bed and dashes for the door. Unfortunately for her, I am always faster, and I manage to hook her foot and trip her, sending her flying straight into the wall.

She hits with a solid thud. I do not even pause, because we do this countless times, and now that she has her wolf, she'll heal faster. I reach the kitchen just a few seconds before she does.

"Honestly, girls, aren't you a little too old for that childish behavior?" Dad scolds. I lean in and give him a quick kiss on the cheek while Mom tells him to leave us alone—it is our birthdays, and we should just eat. Serena and I hide our smirks and stuff our mouths full. Mom can really cook, and I get my skills from her as well.

"What are your plans today, girls?" Mom asks.

"After breakfast, we are going to shift and go for a run," Serena says, "but then we are probably just going to lounge around all day, eat junk food, and watch movies. I hear shifting for the first time completely exhausts you, so we are doing that today so we have energy to dance tomorrow!"

"I know the boys are occupied with pack business today, so it is just you two," Dad says. They are getting everything prepared so Dad and the Alpha can retire and Kaelen and Garrett can assume leadership. Finn has border patrol duty today because he swapped shifts to have tomorrow off, so it is officially a girls' day.

"That is fine," I say, though I feel a little let down. "They would not want to watch our movies anyway." I know Kaelen said he would not see me today, but a part of me still clings to a faint hope.

Chapter 5
Ava's POV

"Hurry, Ava! I need to get going!" Serena states impatiently. I am already feeling slow and heavy, so I am not moving very fast.

"Girl, you have to get going—my tail needs to stretch!" Sable says. I roll my eyes, quickly eat three more bites from my plate, and hand it to my mother so she can clean it.

"Thank you, Mom!"

We dart out the door before she can even form a reply.

Serena rubs her hip as she sprints for the bedroom to get into the shower before me. I let her win because I want five more minutes of rest before our small family celebration.

Soon enough, we are showered, and Serena is fussing over my hair and my makeup. I genuinely dislike applying makeup, and wearing dresses is absolutely not my preference.

"I have to wear a dress tomorrow, so do not put me in one tonight as well! Besides, it is my birthday too, and I choose comfort!" I say firmly.

"Fine, but no sweatpants," Serena retorts, looking determined. Rolling my eyes, I select a pair of black ripped skinny jeans and a cream-colored sweater. Serena wears a long-sleeved dress with a high neckline that ends just above her knees—it is white with yellow flowers scattered across it.

When we enter the kitchen, rich aromas wash over us: pot roast, potatoes, and carrots—one of my most beloved meals. I end up consuming three bowls because getting my wolf makes me ravenously hungry. Dinner proceeds smoothly, filled with light talk and easy conversation.

Serena and I receive matching necklaces featuring a wolf emblem—mine is white gold and hers is yellow gold. Eventually Serena's parents say goodnight, and we go upstairs to bed. It is a wonderful birthday, but I know everything will change tomorrow.

"Happy birthday, beautiful," Kaelen whispers in my mind.

'Oh my god, he sounds delicious,' Sable says. 'Sable!' I scold, laughing even though I secretly agree.

"Thank you! When do I get to see you tomorrow?" I ask.

"Not until the party, unfortunately—I have a few matters I need to finalize," he answers.

"Okay," I say. "Well, I will be the one wearing red."

"Ugh, I will have to kill someone if they look at you—or even touch you," Kaelen says, growling.

"Hmm, we shall see, lover boy," I tease. I need to end this before Serena detects my scent of arousal. She is already looking at me with a knowing grin. She realizes I am mind-linking someone, and the smile on my face tells her exactly who it is.

"Goodnight, my princess," Kaelen says.

"Goodnight, my prince," I reply.

"Sooo, how is Kaelen?" Serena asks as I turn toward her.

"He is so perfect," I admit. "If I am not his mate, I will be utterly heartbroken. I have loved him since we were children. What if I am not his mate and he ends up with someone else?"

"Oh, girl, that is not going to happen," Serena insists. "You two are made for each other. Everyone can see that he loves you too. Even if he had another mate, I bet he would reject her for you. I would wager money on it," she states firmly.

"I do not know," I say. "I just have this terrible feeling. I hope you are right, but I would not allow him to reject his mate if it is not me. That is not right. The mate bond comes from the Moon Goddess herself. I cannot interfere with that." We have been taught our entire lives that nothing is more important than the mate bond. You are supposed to cherish and love your mate. It is what every girl dreams of finding, and we are no exception.

"Well, I think tomorrow is going to be perfect, and we will both find our mates and live happily ever after!" Serena says, but even her voice holds a trace of anxiety.

"You are probably right," I say, rolling over to conclude the conversation.

'Sable… what do I do? What if he is not our mate and my fairytale ends here? What if he is my mate and this bad feeling is something far worse?' I ask inside my head.

'I do not know what will happen tomorrow,' Sable answers, 'but I do know that no matter what, we are strong, and we will endure whatever comes. Nothing breaks us.' Her tone remains even. Then it softens. 'Good night, birthday girl. Tomorrow is going to be a long day as well,' Sable adds gently.

Chapter 6
Ava's POV

BEEP, BEEP, BEEP—my alarm shrills, signaling that it is 9 a.m. We are not required at the pack house until 3 p.m. The celebration is scheduled from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m., after which we will proceed to the pre-prom dinner, with the dance immediately following.

It takes us three hours to get ready, so we still have several hours to kill.

Serena gasps. "Oh my god, I passed everything!" When I glance over, tears are glistening in her eyes. Academics have always been more challenging for her, but she never gives up. She is not a straight-A student, but she never receives a C.

"I passed as well!" I say, feeling a surge of pride.

"Let me guess—probably all A's again," she remarks, sounding slightly exasperated but mostly happy for me.

"Yes, but Yolanda is named valedictorian, and I am perfectly content with that," I say. "No speech required from me!" I laugh, a little disappointed but mostly relieved. Public speaking is absolutely not my strength.

"Let's watch a movie until we need to start getting ready!" Serena proposes.

"Okay. I will collect snacks, and you can select the movie," I tell her.

I return carrying sausage, cheese, and crackers in one hand and chocolate, popcorn, and soda in the other. We spend the entire morning snacking and laughing, feeling so relieved that we passed my classes. I do not even sense my earlier dread anymore!

Before long, Serena is tugging at my hair and attacking my face with makeup. She pulls half my hair back into an elegant braid, leaves pieces to frame my face, curls those strands, and curls the back as well. She gives me a smoky eye and applies only a slight blush because I naturally blush enough as it is.

When I step into my gown and look into the mirror, I barely recognize myself. I look breathtaking. My wolf necklace is what truly completes the entire look. Serena emerges with her hair styled in a low side bun with soft pieces framing her face, and she wears a dark blue smoky eye that complements her dress. She looks like an absolute vision.

"Damn, girl! I am going to be jealous of whoever ends up as your mate!" I declare, clutching my chest as if my heart is breaking.

"Oh my god, Ava, you look even more incredible than I imagined you would," Serena says. "I will take partial credit, of course!"

"Of course you—" I begin.

"Girls, it is time to go! " my mother calls out in a singsong voice, cutting me off. "I cannot wait to see your beautiful dresses!"

"Oh great, " I mutter, grimacing. "She already sounds like she's crying. "

"I heard that—now get out here!" Mom says firmly.

I smirk at Serena, and we proceed into the living room together.

When I see my mother, she is dabbing tears from her face, and my father looks as though he is in agony.

"What is wrong, Dad?" I ask, suddenly somewhat concerned.

"Well, I would prefer turtleneck dresses," he whispers, "but you girls do look beautiful."

"I love you too, Dad," I say.

"Alright, enough of this sentimental stuff—let us get you girls to your birthday party!" Dad announces. He has responsibilities to attend to regardless, so he drives us to the pack house in his truck.

And then I feel it—my dread crashes over me. I attempt to behave normally and keep my heart rate steady, but it accelerates anyway. In the rearview mirror, I catch my father's eyes, and he gives me a questioning look.

'Are you okay?' Dad asks through the mind-link. Fortunately, Serena is too excited to notice anything.

'Yes,' I answer. 'Just a bad feeling about tonight. I am sure it will amount to nothing—you know how those feelings can be,' I add, trying to sound reassuring.

'Hmm. Well, mind-link me if you need me, and I'll be there anytime, sweetie,' he tells me.

'I know. Thank you, Dad. I love you,' I send back.

'I love you too,' he replies.

When we arrive at the pack house, it is already filled with young people. The game room has been transformed into a party space: all the games have been removed, and tables, snacks, and drinks have been set up instead. Alcohol is also present. If you are of legal age—eighteen—you can drink, though it takes a substantial amount to intoxicate a wolf. If you are seventeen or younger, it is not permitted, but it also is not strictly enforced since we are on pack territory. Serena and I head directly for the drinks, and we each pour ourselves one. Serena prefers sweet beverages, so she selects a Sex on the Beach, and I favor whiskey, so I mix myself a Crown and Coke.

"I need to use the bathroom!" Serena shouts over the music.

"Okay—I am right behind you," I answer.

We make it about halfway, and then Serena halts abruptly. She starts sniffing the air and drifting away from the bathrooms. What is happening with her? I try to follow, but she moves too swiftly through the crowd.

With so many people packed into the room, it takes me a moment, but I finally catch up. Serena has this deer-in-the-headlights expression, and she is staring fixedly ahead. I turn my head to see what she is looking at, and it is Kaelen. My stomach plummets and a sinking sensation spreads through me as I hear Serena whisper, "Mate."

No. No, no, no—that cannot be correct. He is supposed to be my mate, not Serena's. I freeze, staring at him. Tears fill my eyes. I do not even breathe, and Kaelen's gaze darts between Serena and me as if he has no idea what to do. Garrett and Finn stand on either side of him, both wearing stunned expressions. No one can believe it. He is supposed to be my mate—MINE.

"Ava, I…" Serena stammers, not sure what to say or how to move. Everyone watches, waiting to see what I will do. When I snap out of my trance, Sable is howling in my head, because she feels my heartbreak as if it were her own. My entire life feels like a deception—every make-out session, every midnight conversation, every moment I believed meant something—obliterated.

Kaelen takes one step toward me, and then a growl cuts through the air, freezing him in place. I look over and see Serena with her hand covering her mouth, her expression shocked. I have told her all my feelings regarding Kaelen; she knows precisely how deeply I love him.

Our friendship will not survive this—I'm sure of that. She is already acting possessive toward him. She is probably terrified he will reject her. And somehow my heart fractures for her as well. She is gazing at a mate who is in love with another girl, and that other girl is her best friend.

The only thing I can think to do is turn and flee—and I run as fast as I can. I hear people yelling my name behind me, and then I hear paws pounding the ground as someone chases me. I shift mid-stride and speed up even more. I manage to outrun everyone.

I allow Sable to take control, and I do nothing but weep—weep for my lost friend and my lost love. Sable finds a cave and crawls inside. I put up a wall around my mind. I cry myself to sleep while blocking out every mind-link that keeps trying to reach me.

title: Your dog drinks less than you think
body:
Your dog drinks from the toilet. From puddles. From the hose. But barely touches the clean bowl you just filled.

#AD 4 days’ worth of meal prep done in 45 minutes using fresh produce from Lidl for under £30
 
Daily Macro Breakdown:
1,495 kcal | 187g carbs | 108g protein | 34g fat

(1) Honey Raspberry Overnight Oats
375 kcal | 54g carbs | 26g protein | 5g fat

Ingredients: 
200g oats
2 x 450g Skyr Icelandic Style Raspberry Yoghurt
250g Fresh Raspberries
40g Runny honey
200ml water (or milk)

Method: 
1. Add 50g oats into each container and mix with 50ml water (milk can also be used). Press into your container to form a base. 
2. Add your 2 x raspberry protein yoghurts 900g total and fresh raspberries into a large mixing bowl and mix until combined. Set aside 12 raspberries for decoration. 
3. Divide the yoghurt mix evenly into 4 jars or containers. Top each with 3 raspberries and a drizzle of 10g honey.
4. Seal and refrigerate overnight. Enjoy! 

(2) Honey Mustard Chicken Pasta Salad
486 kcal | 54g carbs | 39g protein | 13g fat

Ingredients: 
250g pasta
1 red onion
1 cucumber
250g cherry tomatoes 
1 head (600g) of romaine lettuce
600g diced chicken breast 
1 tin (285g) sweetcorn 

Dressing: 
2 tbsp (30g) dijon mustard 
1.5 tbsp (22ml) lemon juice
3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 tbsp (15g) runny honey

Method: 
1. Cook your diced chicken breast (season with salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder) and pasta. 
2. Dice the cucumber, quarter the cherry tomatoes, finely slice the red onion and shred the lettuce. 
3. Make the dressing by whisking together the Dijon mustard, honey, olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper. 
4. Add your cooked and cooled pasta, chicken and then all the veg including the drained sweetcorn into a large salad bowl and pour over the dressing. 
5. Toss until everything is well coated
6. Divide into 5 containers and enjoy!

20 grams feta cheese

¼ avocado
Sat and pepper

Butter or olive oil spray
Lemon juice

6. Mash the avocado onto the tortilla.

8. Garnish with pickled onions and chili oil.

PUMPKIN CHICKPEA CURRY ✨⁠
⁠
This curry is cozy, comforting, and full of nourishment. Tasted and adored by our staff at the JSHealth HQ!⁠
⁠
Made with seasonal pumpkin, aromatic spices, and creamy coconut milk, it’s a plant-based favorite that’s rich in flavor and fiber. We’ve chosen chickpeas for an energizing boost of plant-based protein, however this curry would serve as the perfect base for tofu, chicken, or shrimp. This one is perfect served with fluffy rice or warm naan to soak up every last spoonful!⁠
⁠
Enjoy,⁠ Jess xx⁠
⁠
Time to cook: 15 minutes prep + 45 minutes cooking ⁠
⁠Serves: 4⁠
⁠Ingredients:
1 tbsp coconut oil (or olive oil)
1 tsp black mustard seeds (or ½ tsp ground mustard)
1 medium brown onion, finely diced
3 garlic cloves, minced
1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
½–1 tsp chilli flakes, to taste (optional)
1 ½ tsp ground turmeric
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp ground coriander
~500g pumpkin, peeled & cut into 2–3cm cubes
1 x 400g can chickpeas, drained & rinsed
1 x 400ml can coconut milk (full-fat for creaminess)
1 cup vegetable stock (or water + 1 tsp veggie stock powder)
Salt & pepper, to taste

Method:

Bloom the mustard seeds: Heat the coconut oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and cook until they start to pop (30–60 seconds).

Sauté aromatics: Add onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened. Stir in garlic, ginger, and chilli. Cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.

Toast the spices: Add turmeric and cumin. Stir for 30 seconds to release their aroma.

Add pumpkin: Stir through the pumpkin cubes, coating them in the spice mix.

Simmer: Pour in coconut milk and vegetable stock. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 10–12 minutes until pumpkin is just tender. 

Add chickpeas: Stir in chickpeas and cook uncovered for 5 minutes to let the sauce thicken. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

#asianfood #dinner #healthyeating #healthyliving #healthyrecipe⁠

EASY PRAWN PAELLA ✨⁠
⁠
Meet our twist on the classic prawn paella, with all the same irresistible flavors! ⁠
⁠
This gluten-free recipe is a delicious departure from tradition, offering smoky paprika undertones, and a vibrant medley of aromatic spices. For a vegetarian twist, simply skip the prawn and enhance the dish with hearty lentils or crumbled feta cheese.⁠
⁠
Time to make: 40 minutes⁠
⁠
Serves: 4⁠
⁠
Ingredients:⁠
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil ⁠
4 garlic cloves, minced⁠
220g prawns, deveined and peeled⁠
1 red onion, finely chopped⁠
1 red chilli, finely chopped ⁠
2 tbsp tomato paste⁠
1 tsp paprika ⁠
1 zucchini, chopped ⁠
1 punnet cherry tomatoes⁠
1 ½ cup arborio rice⁠
10 kalamata olives⁠
4 cups vegetable stock⁠
3 cups baby spinach⁠
1 lemon, juiced and zested ⁠
½ bunch chives⁠
¼ cup pine nuts, toasted (omit for nut-free) ⁠
⁠
Method: ⁠
Heat the olive oil in a large lidded fry pan. Add the red onion, chilli, and half the garlic. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Sauté for 3–4 minutes or until the onion has softened and starts to caramelize. Add the tomato paste and paprika and fry for two minutes whilst stirring. Add the zucchini and tomatoes and sauté for 2 minutes. Next add the olives and rice. Pour in the stock, bring to the boil, reduce the heat, and then cover and simmer for 20 minutes. ⁠
⁠
When the rice is almost done, heat 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the remaining garlic to the pan and sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add the prawns and season with sea salt and black pepper. Cook for 3 minutes on one side before flipping and cooking for a further minute. Remove from the pan and set aside. ⁠
⁠
Remove the lid from the rice and add the spinach to the pan. Stir through to wilt. Cover and leave to sit for 5 minutes with the heat off. Remove the lid and add the prawns in and stir to heat. Garnish with lemon juice, chives, and toasted pine nuts. ⁠
⁠
⁠

title: 🔥Don’t pay a cent.✨ Read it all — free, free, free!✨🔥
body:
I, the princess of the Moretti Empire and the DeNucci family’s combined empire, became pregnant with the president of the Princes of Darkness MC., at the age of 21. 
But he betrayed and abandoned me. After that, I left his side and also distanced myself from my family. 
Just when I was about to live a peaceful life, a group of bikers surrounded me, and at the forefront was the man who had hurt me the most—Ryder Savage Jackson......

“Mommy … go.” I push the cart around the store as I watch my beautiful two-year-old daughter Rebel clap her hands as I go faster, and she squeals in delight.
 
She is so much like him. He who shall not be named kind of scenario. She doesn’t take after me much apart from the honey eyes. Her dark blonde hair and nose are like his and boy, does she have his temper.
 
“Ok Rebel, we need to finish this. Then we will go to the park. How does that sound?” she kicks her legs and claps again. I chuckle at her behaviour, leaning down to kiss her head. I finish off shopping and head out to the car.
 
I left home over three years ago. Three years I ran. The same man that is Rebel’s father hurt and humiliated me. I never got to tell him he was about to become a father. The woman he claimed had already done that. I couldn’t risk my parents finding out, either. It would have caused a war between my family and his MC.
 
My dad is the Don of the Moretti empire and my momma, well, she is the head of the cartel and the DeNucci family. I am their only daughter. The princess of the combined empire. My twin brother Nathaniel is next in-line to take the position of Don after dad retires and me well, I was supposed to take over the DeNucci family and my younger brother Nico would take over the cartel.
 
That all went to mess when I ran. It was difficult at first going to a new place. Living not just for myself but for the life I was carrying inside of me. The savings I had I used to find a place to live, get everything we needed and what was left, I invested it in a rundown bar.
 
I changed my name and never looked back. My bar is doing so well and it is nice to know that I have made it what it is today. The bar is called the Eclipse. The town we live in is a tourist town. So we get different people coming and going.
 
Most people come here to the lake in the summer and the skiing in the winter. It’s a friendly and safe place to live and I am happy here. When I first arrived here, I was lost, but I was welcomed and I wouldn’t leave even if you paid me too.
 
Once we have arrived at the house. It’s nothing like the Moretti mansion, but it’s home. With its white picket fence. White walls and blue door. It doesn’t look like much from the outside, but it’s open plan on the inside and modern. Upstairs there are three bedrooms, all with an en-suite and a family bathroom. Rebel has her own room next to mine and life is good.
 
She doesn’t want for anything; I carry the shopping inside and then carry Rebel in. Shutting the door, I place her in the living room with some of her toys as I put the shopping away. Just then, Boomer bounds inside. Rebel loves him as much as he loves her. I got Boomer when I was preqnant and both he and Rebel grew together.
 
He is a beautiful big softy. He is a Cane Corso. He is as black as night with a tiny patch of white on his tʃest. He is our protector, even if he does drool everywhere and talks back when you tell him no.
 
My phone rings and I take it out of my back pocket and see that it is Coral who is supposed to work the bar tonight. I gr0an, knowing she is about to ask me to cover her shift, no doubt because her douchebag ex won’t have their child tonight.
 
“Hey Coral, what’s up?”
 
“Hey Angie, look, I’m really sorry to do this, but Steve ditched me and I can’t find a sitter.” I roll my eyes. If I had a dollar for every time he has let her down over the last year, I would be a wealthy woman.
 
“Ok. Coral, no worries, but you and I need to have a chat about this. I will cover tonight, but you need to sort this out.” I hate being the bad guy, but she knows I have a toddler, too. I don’t have the support she does, even if it is my own doing.
 
“I will get it sorted. I’m so sorry Angie. I promise I will make it up to you.” We say goodbye and end the call. I look at Rebel and sigh. Still time to take the little miss to the park, and then I will have to call Mrs Lawson and see if she is available. I know she will be she loves Rebel.
 
“Boomer, leash.” I say and he is off to get what I’ve asked as I scoop up my now rowdy toddler and get her ready for the park.
 
“Go now?” I smile at her.
 
“Yes, sweetheart, we can go now.” I say, kissing her on her cheek. Grab the stroller and strap her in. Getting her in is always a workout. The child goes as stiff as a board and she finds it hilarious.
 
I make the call to Mrs Lawson as I put the leash on Boomer and pray she can help.
 
“Hello, Angie, how are my two favourite girls today?” I grab my keys and some snacks and drinks, placing them in the changing bag and attach it to the stroller.
 
“We are doing just fine. I hate to do this last minute, but Coral called and …”
 
“Say no more. I will be at your house at seven, then you can head out.” God love this woman. She is my lifeline.
 
“Thank you so much, I hate to spring it last minute.”
 
“Nonsense, sweetheart. You know I love to help out.”
 
“Thank you again, Mrs Lawson. I will see you soon.”
 
“How many times, call me Scar. You are family. No need to thank me. I will see you both soon. Bye Angie.” I hang up and head out.
 
After a couple of hours at the park and one tuckered out Rebel, she is fed and bathed and ready for bed. Mrs Lawson arrives and I head to work.
 
Pulling up at the bar, I notice we are packed out tonight. Well, at least the shift will go quickly.
 
Leaving the car, I head inside. I smile at some of the locals and make my way behind the bar. The night goes smoothly and begins to quiet down. I look at Max and tell him I’m going to office and if he needs me to come get me.
 
I head to the office to get some 0rders done and check the accounts and I lose track of time.
 
“Erm, Ang. I need you back at the bar.” I look up and smile as I stand and leave the office, shutting and locking the door behind me.
 
The music gets louder the closer I get to the bar. The sound of raucous laughter fills the air and something feels off. My gut twists and flutters the closer I get.
 
Stepping out behind the bar, I freeze. No, it can’t be. I notice the cuts.
 
The Princes of Darkness MC with white stitching against the black leather. An embroidered patch of a red devil with wings riding a Harley. The same MC that he runs, the very same MC that is in allegiance with my family. What are they doing this far out?
 
“Angel.” My eyes widen and my heart jumps into my throat as I look into the icy blue eyes of the man who broke my heart, the man who forked his wh0re in front of me, the man I ran from, the father of my daughter.
 
Ryder ‘Savage’ Jackson.

They have found me; they have found me. Crap, frick, tvat! I look at him and I’m having a mini panic attack. All I can see is him and her. The words he spewed at me with such hatred and the smirk on her face. Why is he here?

He reaches for me and I react instantly; I grip his wrist and turn him, shoving his arm up his back. He gr0ans and the men are now on their feet. I look at Blaze, his VP, and he is telling everyone to remain calm.

“You have the wrong person. Now get out.” I shove him forward as the fight-or-flight takes over. I need to get out of here. I need to leave. I need to grab Rebel and Boomer and go. But where?

“Angel, that’s not going to happen. We have been looking for you. Your family has been looking for you. We have found you and there is no running from us,” Savage says to me as I step back, my eyes not leaving his.

“My name isn’t Angel. I don’t even know who you are. Now I won’t ask again. Get the fudge out of my bar or we will have a problem.” My voice is like steel as I stare the fricker down. I won’t back down now. I have to protect my daughter.

I catch movement from the corner of my eye and hold my hand up, and the movement stops. 

Just then, the door opens and more bikers come in, surrounding me completely...
